job.style: a short story with Indian characters in everyday life

passage: Rohan and his father, Mr. Sharma, were discussing the new village council elections in their town. Mr. Sharma explained that India follows a federal structure where power is shared vertically between the Union, State, and local governments. Rohan asked if the state government now loses all its authority to the local panchayat. His father smiled and clarified that decentralisation actually empowers local bodies to handle specific local issues, while the state retains its constitutional responsibilities. They then discussed the national parliament. Rohan wondered if the central government could simply override state laws on any subject. Mr. Sharma corrected him, explaining that the Constitution clearly defines the Union, State, and Concurrent lists, ensuring the centre cannot interfere in state-exclusive matters. Finally, they talked about the national vision. Rohan suggested that since India is a democracy, the majority community should dictate all national policies. Mr. Sharma firmly disagreed, stating that true democracy requires protecting the rights of minorities and sharing power across different groups to prevent the tyranny of the majority. He added that the judiciary, executive, and legislature operate independently at the same level to ensure checks and balances, which is a horizontal distribution of power, distinct from the vertical levels of federalism.

items.evidence: His father smiled and clarified that decentralisation actually empowers local bodies to handle specific local issues, while the state retains its constitutional responsibilities.
items.q: After village councils get more power, what happens to the state government?
options: The state still keeps its constitutional duties
The state gives all its powers to panchayats
The state now appoints every village sarpanch
The state passes its powers up to the centre
items.explain: Local bodies handle local issues, but the state keeps its own constitutional responsibilities.

wrong.why: thinks decentralisation takes away all state power
thinks the state chooses panchayat leaders
mixes up local and central levels

items.evidence: Mr. Sharma corrected him, explaining that the Constitution clearly defines the Union, State, and Concurrent lists, ensuring the centre cannot interfere in state-exclusive matters.
items.q: What stops the central government from overriding a state law on a state-only subject?
options: The subject lists written in the Constitution
The centre's own wish to avoid quarrels
The panchayat's power to block central laws
The majority community's vote in each state
items.explain: The Constitution defines Union, State and Concurrent lists, so the centre cannot interfere in state matters.

wrong.why: thinks the centre can legislate on anything but chooses not to
picks the local body mentioned nearby

items.evidence: Mr. Sharma firmly disagreed, stating that true democracy requires protecting the rights of minorities and sharing power across different groups to prevent the tyranny of the majority.
items.q: Why did Mr. Sharma reject the idea that the majority should decide all national policies?
options: Democracy must safeguard smaller groups' rights too
Democracy must leave all decisions to the courts
Democracy must let each state's majority rule
Democracy must keep all power with the centre
items.explain: True democracy protects minorities and shares power among groups to prevent tyranny of the majority.

wrong.why: misreads checks and balances as courts ruling alone
still believes majority rule is democracy
thinks the centre should control everything

items.evidence: He added that the judiciary, executive, and legislature operate independently at the same level to ensure checks and balances, which is a horizontal distribution of power, distinct from the vertical levels of federalism.
items.q: Which example shows horizontal sharing of power?
options: Courts and lawmakers checking each other's work
Union and states making laws on separate lists
Religious groups sharing seats in the cabinet
Panchayats solving local problems for villages
items.explain: Horizontal sharing is among judiciary, executive and legislature at the same level, giving checks and balances.

wrong.why: thinks horizontal means central and state levels
thinks horizontal means sharing with social groups

items.evidence: Mr. Sharma explained that India follows a federal structure where power is shared vertically between the Union, State, and local governments.
items.q: Rohan's town elects a new village council. Where does this council fit in India's federal structure?
options: At the local level, below Union and State
At the Union level, beside Parliament
At the State level, as a state office
At the same level as the courts
items.explain: Power is shared vertically among Union, State and local governments; a village council is local.

wrong.why: thinks every elected body is national
thinks panchayats are part of state government
mixes up vertical levels with horizontal branches
